sections.sectionTitle: Section A: Themes from the Old Testament

topics.title: Sovereignty of God, Leadership and Parental Responsibility

subtopics.content: God as Creator/Controller, leadership of Joseph, Moses, Joshua, Deborah; Eli and Samuel
subtopics.objective: Understand God's creation and control of the universe (Gen 1-2)[cite: 152]; analyze leadership qualities and roles of Joseph, Moses, Joshua, and Deborah[cite: 152]; evaluate parental responsibilities and consequences of bad parenting through Eli and Samuel[cite: 152].

topics.title: King Saul, David, Solomon, Supremacy of God and Reforms

subtopics.content: Saul's disobedience, David's submission/sin/repentance, Solomon's wisdom/unwise decisions, Ahab, Elijah, Josiah
subtopics.objective: Examine Saul's disobedience and fall[cite: 152]; analyze David's submission to God's will, sin with Bathsheba, repentance, and forgiveness[cite: 152]; evaluate Solomon's wisdom, Rehoboam's foolishness, and kingdom division[cite: 152, 153]; analyze Elijah's contest at Mount Carmel proving God's supremacy[cite: 153]; examine Ahab's and Gehazi's greed[cite: 153]; study King Josiah's religious reforms[cite: 153].

topics.title: Concern for Nation, Faith, Social Justice and Divine Love

subtopics.content: Exile and response (Nehemiah, Ezra), faith in adversity (Daniel), social justice (Amos), divine love (Hosea)
subtopics.objective: Understand the exile and Nehemiah's concern/rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls[cite: 153]; examine faith and courage in Daniel and his companions[cite: 153]; analyze Amos's message on true religion and social justice[cite: 153]; evaluate Hosea's message on God's divine love and forgiveness[cite: 153].

sections.sectionTitle: Section B: Themes from the Synoptic Gospels and the Acts of the Apostles

topics.title: Baptism, Temptation, Discipleship, Forgiveness and Passion Narrative

subtopics.content: Baptism/Temptation of Jesus, call/demands of discipleship, teaching on forgiveness, Gethsemane, trial, crucifixion, resurrection
subtopics.objective: Understand the significance of Jesus's baptism and temptation[cite: 154]; examine the call and stringent demands of discipleship[cite: 154]; study Jesus's teachings on forgiveness[cite: 154]; evaluate the events of Gethsemane, Peter's denial, trials, crucifixion, burial, and resurrection[cite: 154].

topics.title: Early Church Fellowship, Holy Spirit, Gentile Mission and Opposition

subtopics.content: Communal life in early church, Pentecost, Paul's conversion, Gentile mission, opposition to gospel
subtopics.objective: Analyze fellowship, communal living, and challenges in the early Church (Ananias/Sapphira, selection of deacons)[cite: 154]; study the Holy Spirit's descent at Pentecost[cite: 155]; examine the expansion of the Gospel to Gentiles (Peter, Paul)[cite: 155]; evaluate reasons for and responses to early gospel opposition[cite: 155].

sections.sectionTitle: Section C: Themes from Selected Epistles

topics.title: Epistle of James and First Epistle of Peter

subtopics.content: Faith and works, impartiality, effective prayer, good citizenship, Christian living among non-Christians, interpersonal relationships
subtopics.objective: Examine James's teaching on faith versus works, avoiding partiality, and power of prayer[cite: 155]; analyze Peter's instructions on good citizenship, maintaining Christian conduct in a non-Christian society, and humble interpersonal relationships among church leaders and members[cite: 155].
